name: Password
propertyCopy: Size, corner radius, label, placeholder and the reveal toggle are properties of the same component, not separate fields - change them below to check this field's style and states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Password is a text field that masks its characters by default, with a toggle to reveal the value temporarily - used for any secret the user is actively typing, so it stays hidden from anyone glancing at the screen while still letting the user verify what they typed. When to Use Login and sign-up forms - collecting an account password. A PIN code or short secret - still worth masking even if numeric. Changing a password or entering an API key - any value that shouldn't be visible by default. When Not to Use A value that isn't actually secret - use Input - masking non-sensitive data only adds friction. A one-time code delivered separately and meant to be read back to someone - consider whether masking helps or just adds a step; a plain Input or Number field may serve better. Multi-line secret content - Password is single-line only; there's no dedicated masked textarea in this system. Best Practices Always provide the show/hide toggle - masking with no way to verify what was typed increases error rates and failed submissions. Never restrict paste into a password field; blocking paste actively discourages the use of password managers. Show password strength or requirement feedback near the field, not only after a failed submit. Do and Don't Do PasswordAt least 12 characters. States the rule before the user types, and lets them reveal what they entered so a typo is fixable rather than guessable. Don't PasswordPassword does not meet requirements. Hiding the rule until after submission, with no way to see what was typed, makes the user retry blind against a standard they still have not been told. Accessibility The show/hide toggle has an accessible name that reflects its current state ("Show password" / "Hide password"), not just an icon. Toggling visibility keeps keyboard focus on the field, so the user isn't forced to re-locate it. The input still exposes autocomplete hints (current-password / new-password) so password managers can assist correctly.
